claims.statement: OifsSession is a two-variant enum: Direct holds a DiskManager plus an optional background IpcServer (only in Local/Network modes), while Remote forwards every method through send_request. Standalone mode is a SessionMode that produces a Direct session without an IpcServer, not a third enum variant.
A process-wide SESSION_REGISTRY keyed by the canonicalized image path returns a shared, Arc-cloned OifsSession so threads reference one Master with natural reference counting.

Master election is transport-specific: Local mode uses a deterministic Unix Domain Socket in a per-user private runtime directory ($XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/oifs or /tmp/oifs-<uid>/oifs) with mode 0600 socket and 0600 token file, Network mode uses an atomic create_new rendezvous .master file plus a clock-free active Ping/Pong probe to detect a dead master.

IPC messages are length-prefixed Bincode frames (128MB cap); IpcServer::handle_request is the single dispatcher mapping each IpcRequest to a DiskManager call; the server thread uses poll to accept connections and spawns a dedicated worker thread per peer to handle requests.
Remote sessions self-heal: on a connection error they re-run master election up to five times and, if they become the new Master, pin a local DiskManager as dm_fallback to keep serving locally.

The block-level merge policy is enforced by the Master's single DiskManagerInner mutex rather than per-block locks: disjoint byte offsets merge in place, overlapping offsets are last-writer-wins, and compressed writes use multi-frame append or read-modify-recompress.

canonicalize_path follows up to 32 symbolic link hops even for files not yet created on disk, ensuring concurrent threads opening distinct symlinks targeting the same image resolve to identical canonical registry keys without split-brain.

IPC authentication uses a challenge-response handshake with mutual proof: client sends AuthChallenge with nonce, master replies with AuthChallenge containing its nonce, salt, and encrypted flag; both sides compute keyed BLAKE2b MACs over a domain-separated transcript (direction byte prevents tag interchangeability) using either Argon2id(password, salt) for encrypted images or the published session secret for plain images; master proves it holds the same key via AuthVerify, detecting redirection to a fake master; password never travels on the wire.

Poison-recovered locks (lock_unpoisoned, read_unpoisoned) are used for mutexes guarding reconstructible in-memory state (session registry, IPC client pool, auto-defrag config, async flush pending ranges, decoded blob cache) where a panic mid-critical-section cannot leave data inconsistent; propagating poison would permanently brick the subsystem. DiskManagerInner RwLock deliberately propagates poison because a panic there could leave on-disk structures inconsistent.

BoundedInodeCache and ShardedDirCache use 32 shards with Fibonacci hashing (constant 0x517cc1b727220a95) to uniformly distribute inode IDs and directory inode IDs across independent RwLock shards, eliminating lock contention between concurrent operations on different inodes/directories. Consecutive inode IDs never map to the same shard.

BoundedInodeCache uses Second-Chance (Clock) eviction: each cached inode has an atomic referenced bit set on cache hit (Relaxed ordering). When capacity is reached, eviction walks a queue, giving referenced entries a second chance (clears bit, re-queues) and evicts only unreferenced entries. Only a single entry is evicted per overflow (not the entire cache).

Write operations (write_data_with_filters) execute in three stages: Stage 1 acquires a shared read lock for inspection and metadata collection then drops it; Stage 2 performs CPU-bound filter/compress/encrypt work with zero locks held; Stage 3 acquires the exclusive write lock only for block allocation and metadata commit, then releases it before flushing via sync_mutex. Concurrent readers are never blocked by compression/encryption CPU work.

resolve_path_iter and resolve_parent perform zero-allocation path resolution by iterating over &str slices from split('/') without heap allocation. The entire resolution holds a single inner.read() guard. resolve_parent uses rsplit_once('/') to split the path, then delegates the parent portion to resolve_path_iter, returning the final component as an owned String only for the filename.

Transparent failover in Remote sessions caches the filesystem password in a Zeroizing<String> (src/session.rs#L75-L76, #L664) so it can automatically re-authenticate when reconnecting to a new Master after the original Master crashes, without caller intervention.

write_unpoisoned helper (src/lib.rs#L78-L85) is used for write locks on reconstructible in-memory state: sharded directory cache (src/disk/caches.rs#L251, #L257) and FUSE handle/parent maps (src/fuse.rs#L2242-L2272, #L2665-L2670). DiskManagerInner RwLock deliberately does not use write_unpoisoned and propagates poison.

ReadSession holds the filesystem's shared RwLock read guard for its entire lifetime, amortizing lock acquisition across batches of lookups, inode stats, directory listings, and positional reads to eliminate per-call atomic reader-count cache-line contention.

FileReadHandle pins a validated regular file inode within a ReadSession, eliminating both per-call RwLock acquisition and BoundedInodeCache lookups; provides fast single-block mmap_slice and read_at for raw uncompressed files under IoBackend::Mmap.

ChunkReadCache (capacity 8) caches decompressed sub-chunks for seekable 64K files, keyed by (inode_id, chunk_idx, raw_entry_block, valid_len) to eliminate repeated decompression/decryption for small positional reads.

DecodedBlobCache (max 4 entries, 16 MiB each, 32 MiB total) caches fully decoded payloads for non-seekable compressed/encrypted files, keyed by (inode_id, size, compressed_size, first_block, nonce) to detect mutation; eliminates O(calls × file_size) full-file decode cliff for sequential or random sub-file read_at calls.

Write operations use a three-stage out-of-lock pipeline: Stage 1 (shared read lock) inspects metadata and drops the lock; Stage 2 (zero locks) runs filter, compress, encrypt CPU-bound work; Stage 3 (exclusive write lock) verifies inode unchanged, commits blocks, and flushes via sync_mutex after dropping the write lock.

Path resolution via resolve_path_iter iterates over &str slices from split('/') without heap allocation, holding a single inner.read() guard for the entire resolution; resolve_parent reuses the same iterator.

POSIX OpenMode (OpenExisting, CreateNew, CreateOrOpen) is implemented with double-checked locking in directory blocks: under concurrent races on non-existent files, exactly one thread succeeds while contenders receive EEXIST, preventing duplicate directory entries or orphan inodes.

Block-level merge policy: disjoint byte offsets in the same block merge in place; overlapping offsets use Last-Writer-Wins due to exclusive lock serialization; seekable 64K compression uses COW (allocates fresh blocks, atomically swaps ChunkEntry pointer, frees old blocks); stream compression uses append or read-modify-recompress.

FFI exposes lock-free read path via OIFSReadSession (holds ReadSession + pinned DiskManager via Arc<FfiSharedSession> with field drop order guaranteeing read lock lifetime) and OIFSFileHandle (pins FileReadHandle with its own Arc<FfiSharedSession> so parent session destruction does not invalidate file handles).
